headline: House bill to fund Congress's own offices and support agencies for fiscal year 2025 was voted down in July 2024.
what_it_does: This bill would have provided money for fiscal year 2025 to run the House of Representatives and shared offices like the Joint Committee on Taxation and the Office of the Attending Physician. It would also have funded agencies that support Congress, including the Capitol Police, the Congressional Budget Office, the Architect of the Capitol, the Library of Congress, the Government Publishing Office, and the Government Accountability Office. It would not have funded the Senate, which by custom sets its own budget. It would also have set rules and limits on how the money could be used.

who_it_affects.how: Their offices and operations would have been funded for fiscal year 2025.
The force that protects the Capitol and Congress would have received its yearly funding.
Workers at agencies like the Congressional Budget Office, Government Accountability Office, Library of Congress, and Government Publishing Office would have had their agencies funded.

who_it_affects.group: Visitors to the Capitol, including people with disabilities
who_it_affects.how: Funding for the Architect of the Capitol and the Office of Congressional Accessibility Services would have covered upkeep of Capitol buildings and accessibility services.

who_it_affects.group: People and businesses that register copyrights
who_it_affects.how: The Copyright Office, part of the Library of Congress, would have received funding.
